# Repository Guidance

The global Codex guidance applies. This file adds verified, durable facts for
this repository.

## Project map

- This is a single-package Shorts production workspace built with Next.js 16
  App Router, React 19, TypeScript, and Remotion 4.
- `app` owns pages, route handlers, and route-local helpers; `lib` owns domain
  and server logic; `components` contains shared UI; `types` contains shared
  contracts.
- `remotion/index.ts` registers the Remotion root, and `remotion/Root.tsx`
  defines the `StudioShorts` composition.
- Tests are co-located `*.test.ts` or `*.test.tsx` files under `app` and `lib`.
  `scripts/test-codex-local-paths.ts` is the one explicit test outside those
  roots included by the repository test runner.
- Start repository navigation with `README.md`, `docs/CODEX_GUIDE.md`, and
  `docs/OPERATIONS.md`. Use `docs/developer-map.json` for the generated route
  and domain inventory and `docs/environment-map.json` for environment-variable
  usage.
- For Personal V1 product decisions, prefer
  `docs/PERSONAL_V1_FINAL_USER_FLOW.md`,
  `docs/PERSONAL_V1_SCREEN_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md`,
  `docs/PERSONAL_V1_DESKTOP_WIREFRAMES.md`, and
  `docs/PERSONAL_V1_UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` over the older simplification
  blueprint.

## Sources of truth

- `package.json` defines local scripts and dependency versions;
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines the CI runtime and validation sequence.
- `docs/CODEX_GUIDE.md` defines task routing and focused verification seams.
  `docs/OPERATIONS.md` defines runtime, release, authentication, and production
  constraints.
- `supabase/migrations` is the ordered Supabase schema history.
  `scripts/local-postgres-schema.sql` is the schema applied by the local
  PostgreSQL setup script.
- `docs/developer-map.json` and `docs/environment-map.json` are generated by
  `scripts/generate-developer-docs.mjs`.

## Verified commands

Run commands from the repository root. CI uses Node.js 22.

- Reproducible install: `npm ci`
- Local onboarding install: `npm install`
- Development server: `npm run dev`
- Type check: `npm run lint`
- Repository tests: `npm test`
- One test file:
  `node --experimental-strip-types --test --loader ./scripts/ts-paths-loader.mjs ./lib/studio/codex-script-to-json.test.ts`
- Production build: `npm run build`
- Refresh and verify generated maps: `npm run docs:refresh`, then
  `npm run docs:check`
- Native render smoke: `npm run render:smoke`
- Local Codex bridge check: `npm run test:codex-local`
- CI sequence: `npm run docs:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, then
  `npm run build`

Before running the app, supply the required app/session and Supabase variables
listed in `README.md`; use `docs/environment-map.json` for the complete
env-to-file inventory.

## Architecture and change boundaries

- Keep page and HTTP concerns in `app`, reusable domain or server behavior in
  `lib`, cross-page UI in `components`, and shared data contracts in `types`.
- When route, entry-file, domain, or environment-variable usage changes,
  regenerate both generated maps with `npm run docs:refresh`. Do not hand-edit
  `docs/developer-map.json` or `docs/environment-map.json`.
- Render-path changes span `remotion`, `lib/studio` render modules, and the
  corresponding `app/api/studio` handlers; validate the native renderer path in
  addition to focused tests.
- Keep the fixed BGM asset at
  `public/bgm/Tango de la Noche - Wayne Jones.mp3`; the runtime expects that
  exact filename.
- Treat `supabase/migrations` as persistence and security-sensitive history.
  No repository command for applying or validating these migrations is
  documented, so disclose that limitation for database changes.
- Production `APP_BASE_URL` must be the real HTTPS origin and must match the
  Codex and Google OAuth redirect hosts. Do not configure
  `LOCAL_AUTH_BYPASS_*` in production.
- `npm run auth:bootstrap-admin -- --dry-run` only checks provisioning inputs;
  the same command without `--dry-run` provisions an administrator in the
  configured store.
- `npm run local:postgres:setup` pulls or starts Docker PostgreSQL, applies
  `scripts/local-postgres-schema.sql`, creates local data/storage directories,
  and rewrites the local fallback block in `.env.local`.
- `npm run local:postgres:sync` reads configured Supabase tables and the
  `video-assets` bucket using the service-role key, then upserts or downloads
  that data into the configured local PostgreSQL and storage locations.

## Verification by change surface

| Change surface | Minimum focused verification | Broader trigger |
|---|---|---|
| TypeScript module with a co-located test | Run that test file and `npm run lint` | Run `npm test` for shared contracts or cross-domain behavior |
| App route or public API contract | Run the route and related domain tests | Run `npm test` and `npm run build` for shared or externally consumed behavior |
| Docs, routes, or env inventory | `npm run docs:refresh` and `npm run docs:check` | Run CI sequence when code or build inputs also changed |
| Remotion or native render path | Related tests and `npm run render:smoke` | Run `npm run build` for route or bundling changes |
| Local Codex CLI or OAuth bridge | Related co-located tests and `npm run test:codex-local` | Run `npm test` for shared authentication or studio behavior |
| Auth bootstrap | Relevant auth tests and the bootstrap `--dry-run` | Use non-dry-run provisioning only when explicitly required |
| Database or persistence | Related store/route tests and `npm run lint` | Report that no migration-application check is defined; run broader app checks when contracts change |

## Repository-specific review focus

- Confirm changes are placed in the owning route, domain, UI, or shared-type
  layer described in `docs/CODEX_GUIDE.md`.
- Check whether route/env changes refreshed both generated maps.
- Remember that `npm test` discovers co-located tests only under `app` and
  `lib`, plus the explicit local Codex path test.
- For auth, publish, storage, sync, and render changes, identify credentials,
  external writes, and local artifact creation before running operational
  commands.
